title: Cloud-Native & Legacy Modernization
breadcrumb: Services > Cloud, Edge & Platform Engineering > Cloud-Native & Legacy Modernization
meta_description: Cloud-Native & Legacy Modernization from Dataq Software: scope, delivery pattern, platforms and committed outcomes.

blocks.x: Buyers rarely need another definition of cloud-native & legacy modernization. They need to know what ships first, what it touches and how value is proven. That is what this page carries: Retire the legacy tax — strangler-pattern modernization with measurable unit economics.

Legacy modernization fails when it is a rewrite project; it succeeds when it is a strangler-pattern program with business metrics. We decompose monoliths along domain seams (event-storming first), route traffic incrementally, and retire components on a schedule the business can see — each wave priced in reduced maintenance cost, deployment lead time and incident load, not just in technology fashion.

The modernization stack is standard and deliberately plain: containers on Kubernetes, infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD with progressive delivery, observability from day one. For mainframe estates we add automated code analysis, data-state replay testing, and parallel-run verification — because regulated workloads must prove equivalence before cutover, not after an apology.

Cloud-Native & Legacy Modernization delivery today concentrates in Banking & Financial Services, Insurance & Risk, Telecom, Media & Entertainment, Public Sector & Government. The metric is chosen with your finance lead, and the baseline is signed before any build begins.
What ships, in the order it ships:

items: Domain decomposition
event-storming-led seam identification and service boundary design
Strangler migration
traffic-routed incremental cutover with parallel-run verification
Mainframe analysis
automated code and data-state analysis with equivalence testing
Platform standardization
containers, IaC, CI/CD and progressive delivery as defaults
Business-metric tracking
each wave priced in maintenance, lead time and incident load
